assessment.name: Synthetic Birken-like specialty law practice
assessment.context: Fictional specialty professional-services practice serving mission-driven organizations. Values are illustrative and are not claims about Birken Law or any client.

summary.interpretation: Maturity and evidence are reported separately. Neither score is a benchmark or causal finding.

dimensions.label: Acquisition / discovery
observations: Specialized educational content attracts high-intent discovery across several service topics.
risks: Topic visibility may not consistently route people to the best next step.
actions: Connect priority educational journeys to the most relevant service and consultation paths.

dimensions.label: Conversion
observations: Scheduling is available, but multiple systems make funnel interpretation difficult.
risks: Scheduler interaction may be reported as a completed consultation.
actions: Reconcile scheduler records with analytics and define the last reliably measured completed step.

dimensions.label: Lifecycle / follow-up
observations: Pre-consultation and post-consultation follow-up varies by matter and operator.
risks: Prospective clients may receive uneven guidance during a high-anxiety decision.
actions: Map the minimum follow-up sequence from booking through engagement or respectful closeout.

dimensions.label: Customer / patient experience
observations: The practice intends a high-touch experience, but direct journey evidence is limited.
risks: Internal confidence may exceed verified client experience.
actions: Collect structured feedback at two high-friction journey moments.

dimensions.label: Measurement / data quality
observations: Channel and content activity are visible, but completed-booking semantics are inconsistent.
risks: Decision-makers may confuse engagement, intent, and completed conversion.
actions: Publish a measurement dictionary that separates CTA, scheduler start, booking completion, and retained matter.

dimensions.label: CRM / MarTech
observations: Core tools exist, but journey data does not move cleanly across them.
risks: Staff may reconcile records manually or work from conflicting status definitions.
actions: Trace one consultation record end to end and remove the highest-risk manual handoff.

dimensions.label: Organizational / process alignment
observations: Responsibilities are understood informally, with limited documented decision cadence.
risks: Cross-functional improvements may stall between client service, operations, and digital work.
actions: Establish a monthly journey review with one owner, a small scorecard, and explicit decisions.

system_warnings.interpretation: Higher maturity claims elsewhere may be difficult to verify because measurement maturity is low.
Initial demand may be created without a reliable follow-up system, creating avoidable leakage.

limitations: Scores reflect assessor judgment against descriptive anchors.
Default weights are equal and have not been empirically calibrated.
Priority ranking estimates gaps and uncertainty, not financial impact or causality.
The diagnostic is a structured hypothesis generator; validate findings with stakeholders and source systems.
